nl.statement: Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu nonparametric regression world on a compact bivariate random design: a law P of (Y,X) on \\mathbb R \\times \\mathbb R^2 whose DERIVED objects are tied to the law itself — \\mathcal X_P is the support of the X-marginal, f_P IS that marginal's Lebesgue density, \\mu_P IS the continuous version of x \\mapsto \\mathbb E_P[Y \\mid X = x] and \\sigma^2_P IS the continuous version of x \\mapsto \\operatorname{Var}_P(Y \\mid X = x), all realised through the regular conditional kernel of Y given X — together with the class regularity (compact support in [-L,L]^2 with rectifiable boundary, L^{-1} \\le f_P \\le L, \\mu_P in the q-Hölder ball of radius L, L^{-1} \\le \\sigma^2_P \\le L) and i.i.d. sampling (Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n \\sim P^{\\otimes n}. — ROUND-7 REVISION (D-F1) — REUSE-MISFIT REPAIR, and the ONLY thing that moves on this node: the decl cited as certifying the fidelity field (F3) was wrong. `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_condExp` (CondDistrib.lean:321), read in source this round, concerns conditional expectations of INDICATORS of a fixed measurable set — it certifies that condDistrib is a regular conditional DISTRIBUTION, not the (F3) mean equality. THE (F3) ANCHOR IS NOW `ProbabilityTheory.condExp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib'` (CondDistrib.lean:389, verified in source this round): `(hX : Measurable X) (hY_int : Integrable Y mu) : mu[Y | mbeta.comap X] =ᵐ[mu] fun a => ∫ y, y ∂condDistrib Y X mu (X a)`, all six typeclass side conditions on the codomain met at ℝ and the ambient `[IsFiniteMeasure mu]` met by `[IsProbabilityMeasure law]`. INTEGRABILITY DISCHARGE, recorded as the reviewer requires: its explicit hypothesis `Integrable Prod.fst law` comes from the structure's own `sq_integrable : MemLp Prod.fst 2 law` field by `MeasureTheory.MemLp.integrable` (L1Space/Integrable.lean:649, `(hq1 : 1 ≤ q) [IsFiniteMeasure mu] : MemLp f q mu -> Integrable f mu`) at q = 2 — so `sq_integrable` is load-bearing twice over: it blocks the Bochner/variance junk values (as round 6 recorded) AND it is the hypothesis that unlocks the (F3) certificate. ONE BOOKKEEPING SEAM F2 must not fumble: the anchor is stated a.e. under `law` for the composite `x ∘ Prod.snd`, whereas (F3) is stated a.e. under the pushforward `law.map Prod.snd`; `MeasureTheory.ae_map_iff` / `MeasureTheory.ae_of_ae_map` (Map.lean:243/:247, both verified this round, `Prod.snd` being measurable) convert between the two. THE MIS-CITED DECL IS RETAINED WHERE IT FITS: `condDistrib_ae_eq_condExp` certifies that the kernel is a regular conditional distribution, which is what licenses reading (F4) — a functional of the conditional LAW — as Var_P(Y | X = ·); for (F4)'s second-moment half F2 may additionally use `ProbabilityTheory.condExp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib` (:381) at f = fun y => y^2, whose integrability hypothesis is `MeasureTheory.MemLp.integrable_norm_pow` (:202) from the SAME `sq_integrable` field. Nothing else on this node moves: the four fidelity fields, the structure layout, the `define-local` disposition, the PO bypass-justification, `binds_symbols`, and every other reuse anchor are exactly as round 6 left them. PRIOR TEXT (round 6), authoritative except for the two condDistrib citations corrected above: ROUND-6 REVISION (D-E0) — WORLD-FIDELITY REPAIR, the whole point of this round. PRIOR DEFECT (reviewer FLAG-world-infidelity): `CtyLaw` was planned as a bag of INDEPENDENT fields — a measure, a set, and three bare functions f_P, mu_P, sigma_P^2 — with the class then imposing envelopes and Hölder regularity on those functions but NEVER relating them to the measure. Under that encoding a `CtyLaw` could carry any smooth bounded triple beside an unrelated law, the estimand mu_P would not be the regression of the sampled data, and both converse theorems would be about a decorated law rather than about E_P[Y | X = x]. REPAIRED ENCODING, which F2 must follow field for field: `structure CtyLaw` carries (1) `law : Measure (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))` with `[IsProbabilityMeasure law]` — the joint law of (Y,X), sample coordinates ordered as in def:cty-distance-data, which is UNCHANGED; (2) `support : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))` and `density : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ` (the object named f_P); (3) `mu`, `sigmaSq : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ`; and then the FOUR FIDELITY FIELDS that make the world faithful and that are the substance of this repair — (F1) `marginal_eq : law.map Prod.snd = volume.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (support.indicator density x))`, i.e. f_P IS the Lebesgue density of X under P and it vanishes off the support; (F2) `support_closed : IsClosed support` together with `density_pos : ∀ x ∈ support, 0 < density x`, from which the non-node helper `support_eq_measureSupport` proves that `support` IS the topological support of the X-marginal, so \\mathcal X_P is the core's 'support of X under P' rather than an arbitrary labelled set; (F3) `mu_condMean : ∀ᵐ x ∂(law.map Prod.snd), mu x = ∫ y, y ∂((ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib Prod.fst Prod.snd law) x)`; (F4) `sigmaSq_condVar : ∀ᵐ x ∂(law.map Prod.snd), sigmaSq x = ProbabilityTheory.variance id ((ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib Prod.fst Prod.snd law) x)`; plus the integrability field `sq_integrable : MemLp Prod.fst 2 law` WITHOUT which (F3)/(F4) would be silently satisfied by Bochner/variance junk values. The regular-conditional-kernel route is the core's own 'regular conditional distribution of Z_j given (S_j, Omega_j)' idiom and is the one Mathlib supports: `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib (Y := Prod.fst) (X := Prod.snd) law : Kernel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) ℝ` type-checks here because ℝ is standard Borel and nonempty and `law` is finite (signature verified by loogle this round), and — CORRECTED IN ROUND 7, this clause originally named `condDistrib_ae_eq_condExp` — `ProbabilityTheory.condExp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib'` (Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/CondDistrib.lean:389, read in source this round) certifies that (F3) really is E_P[Y | X] rather than a bespoke surrogate, its `Integrable` hypothesis being discharged from `sq_integrable` as above. AE-VERSUS-POINTWISE, the one subtlety F2 must not fumble: (F3)/(F4) hold only a.e. under the X-marginal, whereas the ESTIMAND lives on bd(\\mathcal X_P), a Lebesgue-null set. The class pins the boundary values through CONTINUITY, not through the a.e. relation: since density >= L^{-1} > 0 on the support, every nonempty relatively open subset of the support has positive marginal mass, so a continuous function on the support is determined by its a.e.-class — F2 proves this ONCE as the non-node helper `continuous_version_unique_on_support` in Basic.lean, and it is what makes mu_P(x) at a boundary point a well-defined functional of P (and hence makes the packing lemma's explicit boundary values u_{j,b} the genuine regression values, not a convention). ROUND-10 NEW WORLD (D-J0), the SECOND co-main world: the Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu Assumptions 1-2 potential-outcome geographic-boundary design. A law P carries the triple (Y(0), Y(1), X) on R x R x R^2 together with a KNOWN Borel partition of the compact rectangular support into the two assignment regions A_0,P and A_1,P; the deterministic assignment is T = 1{X in A_1,P}, the observed outcome obeys consistency Y = T Y(1) + (1 - T) Y(0), the potential-outcome regressions mu_t,P and conditional variances sigma^2_t,P are the continuous versions of the conditional mean and variance of Y(t) given X, the known interface B_P = bd(A_0,P) cap bd(A_1,P) is a compact rectifiable interior curve with H^1 mass in [L^{-1}, L], the metric is exactly Euclidean and the kernel is exactly K_square, the armwise conditional absolute (2 + nu)-moment of Y(t) given X = x is bounded by L UNIFORMLY AT EVERY POINT x OF THE SUPPORT, taken against a SELECTED conditional kernel that the law object carries as a primitive (ROUND-12/D-L0: the envelope is a genuine POINTWISE statement about that selected version, not an a.e. statement about an abstract conditional expectation, and the global (2 + nu)-integrability of each arm is a DERIVED bookkeeping consequence rather than a primitive field), and P_12(p, nu, L) is the exact displayed L-uniformized specialization of clauses (i)-(x). This is a DIFFERENT world from S1 and is NOT a subclass of it: S1 has no treatment, no potential outcomes and no assignment geometry, and its target is the observed-outcome regression on the SUPPORT boundary, whereas S5's target is the treatment-effect curve tau_P on the KNOWN INTERIOR interface. The two co-main results therefore share only the ambient rate a_n and the direct-product lemma; nothing settled in S1-S4 moves. — ROUND-12 REVISION (D-L0 finding FLAG-WORLD-F5) -- the ONLY thing that moves on this node, and it moves at the world layer again so that no consumer can bypass it. THE DEFECT, accepted in full: round 11 made `condAbsMoment` a REAL-VALUED FIELD tied to the conditional kernel by the a.e. fidelity field (F5) `∀ᵐ x ∂(law.map score), condAbsMoment t x = ∫ |y|^(2+nu) d(condDistrib (armCoord t) score law) x`, and then let clause (v) and t7 use that identification AT EVERY POINT of the support. An a.e. equality licenses nothing pointwise: `condAbsMoment` is not assumed continuous anywhere in the class (unlike mu and sigmaSq, whose boundary values the S1 pattern pins THROUGH CONTINUITY), so the round-11 world still did not entitle t7 to evaluate the kernel moment at a fixed x, and the winsorization bias remained unprovable as stated. THE REPAIR -- A SELECTED CONDITIONAL KERNEL, carried as a primitive, with the envelope taken on THAT version. `A1A2Law` now carries, per arm, the field `condKer : Bool -> ProbabilityTheory.Kernel Score R` with `[∀ t, IsMarkovKernel (condKer t)]`, together with the SINGLE fidelity field that replaces the round-11 (F5): (F5) `condKer_disint : ∀ t, (law.map score).compProd (condKer t) = law.map (fun w => (score w, armCoord t w))`. That is an EQUALITY OF MEASURES, carrying no a.e. quantifier, and it says exactly that `condKer t` IS a regular conditional distribution of Y(t) given X -- a SELECTED version, chosen once and for all by the law object. `condAbsMoment` is then NOT A FIELD at all but a DEFINITION on the structure, `A1A2Law.condAbsMoment t x := ∫ y, |y| ^ (2 + nu) ∂(P.condKer t x)`, so it has a meaning at EVERY x by construction and clause (v)'s pointwise envelope is a genuine statement about the object t7 integrates. Likewise (F3)/(F4) are RESTATED against the same selected kernel -- `∀ᵐ x, muPO t x = ∫ y ∂(condKer t x)` and `∀ᵐ x, sigmaSqPO t x = variance id (condKer t x)` -- so the world carries ONE kernel and F2 must not mint a second. THE TWO-WAY BRIDGE TO `condDistrib`, verified in source this round, is what makes this a free repair rather than a new primitive: forwards, `ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib_ae_eq_of_measure_eq_compProd_of_measurable` (Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/CondDistrib.lean:147, `(hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) {kappa} [IsFiniteKernel kappa] (hkappa : mu.map (fun x => (X x, Y x)) = mu.map X ⊗ₘ kappa) : condDistrib Y X mu =ᵐ[mu.map X] kappa`) turns (F5) into the a.e. identification with `condDistrib`, so every earlier round's condDistrib-anchored reasoning (including `condDistrib_ae_eq_condExp` as the regular-conditional-distribution certificate and `condExp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib`/`'` as the mean anchors) survives verbatim; backwards, `MeasureTheory.Measure.compProd_congr` (Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/Composition/MeasureCompProd.lean, `(h : kappa =ᵐ[mu] eta) : mu.compProd kappa = mu.compProd eta`) shows that ANY a.e.-modification of `condDistrib` satisfies (F5), so requiring a selected version restricts NOTHING about which laws inhabit the world -- it only forces the law object to name the version its envelope is stated against, which is precisely the missing content the reviewer identified. `ProbabilityTheory.compProd_map_condDistrib` remains the disintegration used to integrate a pointwise bound back to a global one. \[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)=\bigl\{P:\text{conditions (i)--(iv) below hold}\bigr\}.\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\): for every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under \(P\) in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\): \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on its compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), with \(L^{-1}\leq\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq L\), and \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a rectifiable curve.  Condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\): \(\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\): \(\sigma_P^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\) and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma_P^2(x)\leq L\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).
nl.frozen_body:
For \(q\in\mathbb N\) and \(L\in\mathbb R\), the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) consists of all random-design regression laws \(P\) satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter regime.)} \(1\leq q\) and \(4\leq L\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \(P\) is a probability law for one observation \((Y,X)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\), \(Y\) is square-integrable under \(P\), and for every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are sampled independently and identically from \(P\).
\item \textbf{(Design.)} The \(X\)-marginal has Lebesgue density \(f_P\mathbf 1_{\mathcal X_P}\), where \(\mathcal X_P\) is the exact topological support of the \(X\)-marginal. Write \(f_P\) for this density. It is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), \(\mathcal X_P\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), and
\[
L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L
\]
for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\). The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) admits a Lipschitz parametrization by \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Regression.)} The function \(\mu_P\) is an \(X\)-marginal-almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\) and belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).
\item \textbf{(Variance.)} The function \(\sigma_P^2\) is an \(X\)-marginal-almost-everywhere version of \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)\), is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), and satisfies
\[
L^{-1}\leq \sigma_P^2(x)\leq L
\]
for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)
=
\{P:\text{\(P\) satisfies the conditions above}\}.
\]

The extra conjuncts `1 ≤ q` and `4 ≤ L` are exactly the core symbol table's declared spaces (q ∈ ℕ with q≥1; L ∈ [4,∞)), i.e. the paper's global background, so the extension coincides on the paper's domain; they also cannot launder the converse (an empty class would send the sup, hence the risk, to 0 and falsify the lower bound).

For a represented rule, write \(T_n\) for its selected law-independent measurable map.
\[
 \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}
 =\left\{\widehat\mu_n:\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there exists a measurable map, denoted }T_n:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\to\mathbb R
 \text{ selected independently of }P,\\

review.note: Unfolding signedDistance, knownGeometry, observedOutcome, treatment, and causalScore gives exactly ((Y_i,(1_{A1}(X_i)-1_{A0}(X_i))‖X_i-x‖₂))_{i≤n}; totalization to all x is conservative because the paper-facing decision class and loss consume it only for x in P.boundary.

nl.statement:
For integers \(p\geq0\), real numbers \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), let \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) be the set of laws \(P\) satisfying all the following member properties.

Write \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\) for the sampled potential outcomes of observation \(i\).

\(\mathrm{(i)}\) For every \(n\), the vectors \((Y_i(0),Y_i(1),X_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq n\), are independently and identically distributed; \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_{1,P}\}\); and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

\(\mathrm{(ii)}\) The support has the rectangular form \(\mathcal X_P=[\underline x_P,\overline x_P]^2\subseteq[-L,L]^2\).  The variable \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), such that \(L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L\) for all \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(iii)}\) For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mu_{t,P}(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) has a \(C^{p+1}\) extension to an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal X_P\), and
\[
 \max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}|\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 +\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\neq z\in\mathcal X_P}
 { |\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)-\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(z)|\over\lVert x-z\rVert_2}
 \leq L.
\]

\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) For each \(t\), \(\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)\) is continuous and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)\leq L\) on \(\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(v)}\) For each \(t\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^{2+\nu}\mid X=x]\leq L.
\]

Write \(\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\) for the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the common interface.

\(\mathrm{(vi)}\) The sets \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) form a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), and their known common interface \(\mathcal B_P\subset\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a compact rectifiable curve satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\leq L\).

\(\mathrm{(vii)}\) The known metric is exactly Euclidean, \(d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\), and the known kernel is \(K_\square\).  The collection
\[
 \{\{z\in\mathcal X_P:\lVert z-x\rVert_2\leq r\}:x\in\mathcal X_P, r\geq0\}
\]
is a VC class with VC index at most four.

\(\mathrm{(viii)}\) Put \(r_p(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(I_1=[0,\infty)\), \(I_0=(-\infty,0)\), and
\[
 \Psi_{t,P,x}(h)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 {1\over h^2}\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)^\top
 \right].
\]
For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Psi_{t,P,x}(h))\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(ix)}\) For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 {1\over h^2}\int_{\mathcal A_{t,P}}
 K_\square(\{(2t-1)\lVert z-x\rVert_2\}/h)\,dz\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(x)}\) For every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), both \(t\), and every \(0<s\leq L^{-1}\), the one-dimensional Hausdorff integral of \(f_P\) over
\[
 \{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}:\lVert z-x\rVert_2=s\}
\]
is finite and strictly positive.

This is the exact displayed \(L\)-uniformized Euclidean-distance, uniform-kernel specialization of CTY Assumptions~1--2, augmented by the displayed Theorem-2 envelope restrictions and quantitative small-bandwidth thresholds.  It is not CTY's entire metric/kernel regime.

review.note: Unfolding A1A2ClassWitness gives the same ten member conditions; the existential disintegration witness conservatively selects pointwise conditional-mean, variance, and moment versions without restricting the underlying law.

nl.statement:
Let \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\) be the class of rules for which there is one collection
\[
 \{T_{n,G,x}:G\text{ is an admissible known geometry},\ x\in\mathbb R^2\}
\]
selected independently of the unknown member law, such that every fixed \((G,x)\) section is a Borel map from \((\mathbb R\times\mathbb R)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\) and
\[
 \widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)=T_{n,G_P,x}(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)),
 \qquad P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L),\quad p\geq0,\quad x\in\mathcal B_P.
\]
No joint measurability, continuity, common modulus, or other regularity in \(x\) is imposed.

review.note: The existential A1A2PIRule is one law-independent collection with every fixed geometry-point section Borel, and its equality is imposed for every admissible law and boundary point with no joint regularity requirement.

nl.statement:
Using the outer expectation \(\mathbb E_P^*\) defined in \cref{obj:def:point-indexed-distance-risk}, for \(p\geq0\) the signed-distance minimax risk is
\[
 R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)=
 \inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right].
\]

review.note: The nested infima and suprema restrict exactly to the decision and law classes, while a1a2BoundaryLoss and outerLIntegral encode the boundary supremum and pointwise-majorant outer expectation.

nl.statement:
For \(B\in\mathbb R\), define the winsorization map
\[
 \psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}.
\]
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), query point \(x\), and bandwidth parameter \(h\), set
\[
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and, with \(B(h)=h^{-1/3}\),
\[
 \widehat m^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)\psi_{B(h)}(Y_i).
\]
Define
\[
 \widehat\beta^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)^{-1}\widehat m^B_{t,x}(h),
 & \forall v\in\mathbb R^{p+1},\ (2L)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^p v_j^2\leq v^\top\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)v,\\
 0,
 & \neg\!\left(\forall v\in\mathbb R^{p+1},\ (2L)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^p v_j^2\leq v^\top\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)v\right).
 \end{cases}
\]
With \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), define
\[
 \widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =
 \max\!\left\{-2L,\min\!\left\{2L,
 e_1^\top(\widehat\beta^B_{1,x}(h)-\widehat\beta^B_{0,x}(h))
 \right\}\right\}.
\]

review.note: On the stated h>0 and L≥4 domain, unfolding the empirical Gram, score, guard, winsorization, and clip gives the displayed estimator, and stabilizedLocalPolynomial_mem derives its law-independent sectionwise-Borel class membership.

nl.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq\frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
Along any sequence with \(M=M_n\to\infty\) and fixed \(\kappa<1\), this lower bound is \(1/2-o(1)\).
nl.frozen_body:
Fix an integer \(M\geq 1\). Assume the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Spaces.)} The spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) are standard Borel.
\item \textbf{(Binary coordinates.)} The variables \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) are independent and uniformly distributed on \(\{0,1\}\).
\item \textbf{(Conditional product structure.)} Conditionally on \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\), the variables \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) are independent, the law of \(Z_j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and the law of \(Z_0\) is independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).
\item \textbf{(Compressed coordinate decoding.)} For each \(j\), \(S_j=c_j(Z_j)\) for a measurable map \(c_j\). The decoder \(\widehat\Omega_j\) is a measurable \(\{0,1\}\)-valued function of \((S_j,(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M),Z_0)\) and is unchanged when its raw coordinate vector is altered only in coordinate \(j\) while \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\) is fixed. Define
\[
 Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b),
 \qquad
 \rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then every such decentralized decoder satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq
 \frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
Moreover, for every real \(\kappa<1\), if
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq \max\{\kappa\log M,0\}
 \qquad\text{for all }j,
\]
then
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq
 \frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]

review.note: Unfolding the named definitions gives the uniform-bit product experiment with A representing Z₀, measurable local compression, decoder invariance to Z_j beyond S_j, ρ_j = 1 − TV, and exactly the stated overlap and KL error bounds; the numerical asymptotic sentence follows from the displayed finite-M bound.

nl.statement:
For every \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on \(q\) and \(L\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), there exist \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) points \(x_1,\ldots,x_{M_n}\) on the boundary of the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), separated by at least a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), a radius \(w_n\asymp a_n^{1/q}\), and laws \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), with the following properties.  Every law has support \(S\), a continuous density \(f_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_{P_\omega}\leq L\), a regression \(\mu_{P_\omega}\) in the stated \(q\)-H\"older ball, and a continuous conditional variance \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\leq L\).  The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\) is rectifiable and the observations are independently and identically distributed.  The half-discs
\[
 C_j=B_2(x_j,w_n)\cap S,\qquad 1\leq j\leq M_n,
\]
are pairwise disjoint.  The subprobability law \(P_\omega\{(Y,X)\in\cdot,\ X\in C_j\}\) depends on \(\omega\) only through \(\omega_j\); the subprobability law \(P_\omega\{(Y,X)\in\cdot,\ X\in S\setminus\bigcup_{k=1}^{M_n}C_k\}\) is independent of \(\omega\); and \(P_\omega(X\in C_j)=m_n\) for one common number \(m_n\) independent of \(j\) and \(\omega\).  There are numbers \(u_{j,0},u_{j,1}\) such that
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)=u_{j,\omega_j},
 \qquad |u_{j,1}-u_{j,0}|\geq c_1a_n.
\]
If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then the laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree, the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]

review.note: AngularPackingAt unfolds to fixed positive constants outside n, eventual square-boundary centers with the required cardinality, separation and radius scales, disjoint half-discs, admissible iid CTY laws, common cell mass, cellwise and off-cell locality, center-value separation, equal radial laws, equality of radial-outcome laws beyond a constant times a_n, and the stated compressed-sample KL bound.

Unfolding ctyDistanceRisk, boundaryLoss, CtyDistanceDecisionClass, scaledRisk, normalizedRisk, and frontierRate gives exactly the displayed common-map infimum–supremum boundary risk, the two eventually equal normalizations by (n/log n)^(1/4) and a_n=(log n/n)^(1/4), and the same positive existential lower bound for each integer q≥1 and L≥4.

The elaborated ⊂ is strict set inclusion, and unfolding both decision classes yields exactly the common law-independent measurable distance map and the law-independent point-indexed family with only sectionwise measurability, under the stated n, q, and L regimes.

Unfolding the risk, decision class, outer integral, and rate gives exactly the paper's inf–sup outer-expectation boundary risk and both equivalent normalizations, with q∈ℕ, q≥1, L≥4, and a positive q,L-dependent lower-bound constant; strict enlargement is independently established by common_map_strict_in_point_indexed.

nl.statement:
Under CTY Assumptions~1(i)--(iii) and 2(i), (ii), and (v), the causal boundary treatment-effect curve is identified by the signed-distance conditional limits:
\[
 \tau_P(x)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D^{\pm}_{P,x}=r]
 -\lim_{r\uparrow0}\mathbb E_P[Y\mid D^{\pm}_{P,x}=r],
 \qquad x\in\mathcal B_P.
\]

review.note: CtyIdentificationAssumptions self-containedly encodes the cited Assumptions 1(i)–(iii) and 2(i),(ii),(v), and the existential source-coherent conditional-mean versions have exactly the cited right- and left-limit identification equality.

nl.statement:
Fix an integer \(p\geq0\), a number \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\).  For \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(h>0\), let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\in\mathbb R^{p+1}\) solve the original, unwinsorized population normal equations
\[
 \Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)
 =\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 {1\over h^2}\mathbf1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)Y
 \right],
\]
and put \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\).  There is a constant \(C=C(p,L)<\infty\) such that, for every deterministic sequence \((h_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfying \(h_n>0\), \(h_n\downarrow0\), and \(nh_n^2\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \left|
 e_1^\top\{\beta^*_{1,P,x}(h_n)-\beta^*_{0,P,x}(h_n)\}-\tau_P(x)
 \right|
 \leq Ch_n.
\]

review.note: Unfolding the bias ratio, population coefficient, score, Gram matrix, and A1A2Class yields the uniform upper-bias claim on the exact Euclidean/uniform-kernel P₁₂ specialization; existential eventual boundedness is equivalent to a finite limsup bound after enlarging the common constant.

nl.statement:
For the degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial score and Gram processes with the fixed uniform kernel, the expected uniform deviations over \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), both arms, and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{t,x}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)-\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert\right]
 \leq C\sqrt{{\log(1/h)\over nh^2}},
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{t,x}\lVert\widehat O_{t,x}(h)\rVert\right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \sqrt{{\log(1/h)\over nh^2}}
 +{\log(1/h)\over n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h^2}
 \right\},
\]
whenever \(h\downarrow0\) and \(n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h^2/\log(1/h)\to\infty\).  The constant \(C\) depends only on the uniform class constants and \(p\).

review.note: Unfolding both deviation functionals and causalSampleLaw gives the expected outer uniform Gram-entry and centered raw-score suprema over both arms and the boundary; finite-dimensional norm equivalence is absorbed in the p-dependent existential constant.

nl.statement: The collection of all closed Euclidean balls in \(\mathbb R^2\) is a VC class with VC index at most four.  Hence the fixed Euclidean metric and uniform kernel in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\) satisfy the actual VC alternative in CTY Assumption~2(iii), uniformly over every member law.

review.note: EuclideanBallsVCProperty unfolds to non-shattering by closed planar Euclidean balls for every finite set of cardinality at least four, exactly VC index at most four; restriction to each member support and the fixed uniform-kernel sublevel sets adds no content.

nl.statement:
For \(B\geq1\), define \(\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}\).  If \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) with \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), then, for both \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_P\!\left[Y(t)-\psi_B\{Y(t)\}\mid X=x\right]\right|
 \leq L B^{-3}.
\]

review.note: A1A2Class supplies ν≥2, L≥4, and the pointwise selected conditional-law moment bound; on x∈P.support the difference of the two integrals equals the paper's conditional expectation of Y(t)−ψ_B(Y(t)), with the required bound L·B⁻³.

nl.statement:
Let \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), \(L\geq4\), \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), \(n\geq1\), \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), and \(B\geq1\).  Let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\) solve the original, unwinsorized population normal equations, and define
\[
 \widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)={1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 \left[\psi_B(Y_i)-r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\right].
\]
There is a constant \(C=C(p,L)\) such that
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \left\|\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)-\mathbb E_P\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)\right\|
 \right]
 \leq C\left\{
 \sqrt{{\log(B/h)\over nh^2}}+{B\log(B/h)\over nh^2}
 \right\}.
\]
This is a direct bounded-envelope adaptation of the expected maximal-inequality arguments in Supplemental Appendix SA-8.3 (Proof of Lemma SA-3), printed pp. 32--33, and SA-8.4 (Proof of Lemma SA-4), printed pp. 33--35, of Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, not a verbatim theorem attributed to them.

review.note: Unfolding winsorizedScoreDeviation and winsorizedCenteredScore gives exactly the supremum of the centered winsorized residual score using the original population coefficient; outerLIntegral is the outer expectation, and the existential constant is uniform in ν,P,n,h,B and depends only on p,L as stated.

nl.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq0\) and every \(\nu\geq2\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\geq48\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\) and all sufficiently small \(\Delta>0\), the class \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) contains a hypercube \(\{P_\omega:\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\}\) with common known geometry
\[
 \mathcal X=[-3,3]^2,
 \quad \mathcal A_1=[-1,1]\times[0,2],
 \quad \mathcal A_0=\mathcal X\setminus\mathcal A_1,
 \quad \mathcal B=\partial\mathcal A_1,
\]
Euclidean distance, and \(K_\square\).  Writing \(q=p+1\geq1\), the family has \(M\geq c\Delta^{-1/q}\) disjoint disks \(S_j=B_2(x_j,w)\), with \(x_j\) on the middle of the bottom edge and \(w=A\Delta^{1/q}\), and satisfies: \(\mathrm{(a)}\) every member obeys every clause of \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\); \(\mathrm{(b)}\) the cell probabilities are bit-independent and equal to \(\rho=\pi w^2/36\), the law restricted to \(S_j\) depends only on \(\omega_j\), and the law outside \(\bigcup_jS_j\) is bit-independent; \(\mathrm{(c)}\) adjacent vertices satisfy \(|\tau_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\tau_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)|=\Delta\); and \(\mathrm{(d)}\), conditional on \(X\in S_j\), the adjacent one-observation signed-distance laws \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) have the same signed-radius marginal, agree outside \(0<D^{\pm}_{P,x_j}<2C\Delta\), and obey in both orientations
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq C_0{\Delta^4\over w^2}.
\]
The constants are independent of \(M\), \(\omega\), \(\Delta\), and \(n\).  When \(p=0\), the constants are chosen with \(A>2C\), so \(2C\Delta<w=A\Delta\).

review.note: Unfolding A1A2HypercubeAt and A1A2Class yields the same quantifier dependencies, fixed geometry, class membership, packing rate, bit locality, target separation, conditional signed-law agreement, two directed KL bounds, and p=0 constraint as the paper statement.

nl.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq0\) and every \(\nu\geq2\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\), there is \(c=c(p,\nu,L)>0\) satisfying
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\left({n\over\log n}\right)^{1/4}R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\geq c.
\]
The conclusion holds for arbitrary law-independent known-geometry point-indexed families with Borel fixed sections, under outer expectation and without joint regularity in the boundary index.  The hard subclass has one fixed support, one fixed known assignment rectangle, and one fixed known interior treatment boundary.

review.note: Unfolding the risks and normalizations gives the stated outer-expectation inf-sup risk over law-independent point-indexed rules with Borel fixed sections; eventual equality of scaledRisk and normalizedRisk makes the displayed bounds equivalent, the threshold may equivalently be enlarged to L0≥48, and the fixed-geometry conjunct records the claimed common support, assignment rectangle, and interior boundary hard subclass.

nl.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq0\), every \(\nu\geq2\), and every \(L\geq4\), the explicit winsorized, Gram-stabilized estimator in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}stabilized\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}estimator}\), with \(h_n=a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) and \(B_n=a_n^{-1/3}\), satisfies, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 |\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq Ca_n.

\begin{itemize}

\[
\tau_P(x)=\lim_{u\downarrow 0}\theta_1(u)-\lim_{u\uparrow 0}\theta_0(u).
\]
\item \textbf{(Uniform first-order bias.)} There is a constant depending only on \(p\) and \(L\) such that, uniformly over every \(\nu'\geq 2\) and every positive antitone deterministic bandwidth sequence \(h_n\to0\) with \(n h_n^2\to\infty\), the finite limsup of the normalized uniform first-order bias ratio is bounded by that constant.
\item \textbf{(Expected maximal bounds.)} For this \(p,\nu,L\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{max}}>0\) such that, along every positive bandwidth sequence \(h_n\to0\) with
\[
\frac{n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h_n^2}{\log(h_n^{-1})}\to\infty,
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), the expected outer Gram-deviation supremum satisfies
\[
\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
\sup_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}\sup_{j,k}
\left|\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h_n)_{jk}-\Psi_{t,P,x}(h_n)_{jk}\right|
\right]
\leq
C_{\mathrm{max}}
\sqrt{\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n h_n^2}},
\]
and the expected outer centered raw-score supremum satisfies
\[

\sup_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
\left\|\widehat m_{t,x}(h_n)-m_{t,P,x}(h_n)\right\|
\right]
\leq
C_{\mathrm{max}}\left(
\sqrt{\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n h_n^2}}
+
\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h_n^2}
\right).
\]

\]
